title: Lemon unlocks plant iron
frame1Text: Add citrus. Get the most from beans.
armature: Plant iron is hard to absorb, but vitamin C unlocks it: a squeeze of lemon (or peppers and tomatoes) with beans and lentils means more iron for your body.

scenes.title: Add citrus. Get the most from beans.
scenes.narration: Did you know that squeezing lemon on your food can help your body absorb more iron?

scenes.label: where the iron is
scenes.title: Plant sources
scenes.narration: Foods like beans, lentils, and spinach contain iron.

scenes.title: Locked.
scenes.narration: But your body has a harder time absorbing iron from plants.
sources: Hurrell & Egli, Am J Clin Nutr 2010: non-heme (plant) iron is absorbed less efficiently than heme iron

scenes.label: — the fix
scenes.title: The key: a lemon.
scenes.narration: That's where vitamin C comes in!

scenes.title: Unlocked.
scenes.narration: It helps your body absorb more of that iron.
sources: Hallberg et al. 1989; Teucher et al. 2004: ascorbic acid enhances non-heme iron absorption

scenes.title: Try it tonight:
scenes.narration: So next time you eat beans, add some lemon.

scenes.title: No lemon? Try:
scenes.narration: Or pair your lentils with bell peppers or tomatoes.

scenes.title: Follow Hello Nutrition AI
scenes.narration: Follow Hello Nutrition AI for more nutrition tips!

sources: Hallberg L., Brune M., Rossander L. The role of vitamin C in iron absorption. Int J Vitam Nutr Res Suppl. 1989;30:103-108 (ascorbic acid increases non-heme iron absorption dose-dependently).
Teucher B., Olivares M., Cori H. Enhancers of iron absorption: ascorbic acid and other organic acids. Int J Vitam Nutr Res. 2004;74(6):403-419.
Hurrell R., Egli I. Iron bioavailability and dietary reference values. Am J Clin Nutr. 2010;91(5):1461S-1467S (non-heme iron from plants is absorbed less efficiently than heme iron).
